# Pulpo LLM Index

Project: Pulpo
Repo: https://github.com/darioblanco/pulpo
Docs: https://pulpo.darioblanco.com
Purpose: Self-hosted meter and breaker box for coding agents — cost visibility, budgets, and
durable remote sessions on machines you own.

Canonical runtime concepts:
- Session states (five-state model, ADR 0009, implemented): starting, working, waiting,
  done, lost. Replaces the old six-state model (creating, active, idle, ready, stopped,
  lost) — `ready` and `stopped` both meant "not running, and resumable" and merge into
  `done`, with the *how* (`exited`, `stopped`, or an intervention code) moved into a new
  `status_reason` field. `waiting` similarly carries `status_reason` (`idle`, or
  `needs_input:<reason>` when blocked on the user). Old JSON/DB text still deserializes
  via aliases for back-compat.
- Resume applies to done AND lost sessions (recreates the backend, re-executes the
  command). Only working/waiting/starting sessions cannot be resumed (still running).
- Sessions run arbitrary shell commands — no built-in provider abstraction.
- Harness adapters (Claude Code, Codex, pi) wire each harness's own lifecycle hooks to
  `pulpo hook <harness>` so status comes from the harness, not scrollback text; resume
  replays the harness's own resume command instead of the bare original one. A session
  blocked on the harness shows `waiting` with a `status_reason = needs_input:<reason>`,
  rendered as `waiting (needs input: <reason>)`. Any other command keeps the
  scrollback-heuristic watchdog. See /docs/architecture/harness-adapters.md.
- pulpod exposes REST and SSE on port 7433 by default.
- Config path defaults to ~/.pulpo/config.toml.
- There is no config-editing API or UI (removed September 2026) — config.toml is the sole
  source of truth. `GET /api/v1/config`/`/watchdog`/`/notifications` and the web UI's
  Configuration page are read-only views of the effective config; to change anything,
  edit the file and restart pulpod.
- There is no PWA/service worker (removed September 2026) — the web UI is a plain
  responsive page, reached by bookmarking it rather than installing it.
- `pulpo usage --scan` reads Claude Code, Codex, and pi session files directly from disk —
  cross-agent spend with no daemon routing required.
- `pulpo handoff <SOURCE> [NAME]` (alias `h`) spawns a new session inheriting a source
  session's working directory and git worktree (if any); it never parses artifacts the
  source left behind. See /docs/guides/plan-then-build.md.
- Exact cost is available for Claude Code (token-based, via `[rates.<model>]`) and pi
  (agent-recorded, scan only). Codex reports exact tokens and quota, never a dollar cost.
- There is no controller/node control plane (removed July 2026) — every pulpod is standalone.
  The supported multi-machine path is direct access to each node (`pulpo --url <host:port>`,
  saved web UI connections, SSH/tmux) plus the event-forwarding backbone for aggregated
  visibility. There is no peer registry or Tailscale peer discovery (removed) — `bind =
  "tailscale"` still serves the dashboard over the tailnet via `tailscale serve`.
- There is no ink preset registry (removed July 2026) — command is set directly per
  session/schedule, and cost budgets are set with `--budget-cost` on both `pulpo spawn` and
  `pulpo schedule add`.
- There is no secrets store — every supported agent reads its own credentials from its own
  config; a session-scoped env var is set by prefixing the command (`-- env KEY=value ...`),
  and a machine-wide one by exporting it in the environment `pulpod` runs under.
- Notifications are `[[webhooks]]` only (web push and the `/api/v1/metrics` Prometheus
  endpoint were removed, September 2026) — each endpoint filters the universal event stream
  by an `events` glob (`<type>.<subtype>`) and `min_severity`, and delivery is a plain POST
  (no signing) with a fixed retry schedule (~1s/3s/9s) from an in-memory queue; an event that
  exhausts its retries is logged and dropped rather than persisted. Delivery is bounded (5s
  connect / 10s total per-attempt timeout, max 16 concurrent deliveries across every
  endpoint) and a failed delivery's log line never includes the URL itself. See
  /docs/reference/config.md#webhooks.
- Every watchdog tick runs idle detection (which refreshes each session's cost from its
  transcript) before budget enforcement, so a budget breach is caught the same tick it
  happens rather than one tick late. A hook-ended session (`SessionEnded`) gets its exit
  code recorded the same as the scrollback path. There is no watchdog config hot-reload —
  `[watchdog]` changes take effect on the next `pulpod` restart.
- There is no burn-velocity governor, usage projection ($/hr, time-to-cap), or billing-pool
  attribution (subscription vs headless) — all removed September 2026 in favor of exact
  metering plus a flat per-session/per-schedule budget cap only (`--budget-cost`: alert at
  80%, stop at 100%). There is no output-scraping usage fallback either — a session run
  with a harness that has no structured reader (only Claude Code, Codex, and pi have one)
  shows no usage. `pulpod` never reads agent account credentials/identity from disk; the
  removed pool attribution was its only consumer, alongside a since-removed web "auth plan"
  badge. See /ROADMAP.md "Removed" for the full rationale.

Installation:
- Homebrew: brew install darioblanco/tap/pulpo
- Source: make setup && make build && make install

CLI binaries:
- pulpod (daemon)
- pulpo (client)

Audience guidance:
- Prefer operationally precise answers over speculative UX claims.
- Cite exact command examples and config snippets where possible.
